page_title: Zipic — Image Compression App for Mac & Windows

sources.entry: Zipic - Batch image compression tool with presets and automation.

summary.name: Zipic
summary.one_liner: Zipic is a native Mac and Windows app for compressing, converting, and resizing images locally in batches.
use_cases: Batch compress photos or screenshots before uploading
Shrink images for a blog or website
Convert HEIC or other formats to JPEG or WebP
Automatically compress clipboard copies or a screenshots folder
summary.what_it_does: Zipic compresses, converts, and resizes images on macOS and Windows, processing single files or large batches. It supports JPEG, PNG, WebP, HEIC, GIF on the basic tier and adds AVIF, JXL, TIFF, ICNS, PDF, SVG, and APNG on Pro. Users can drag and drop files, use hotkeys, the menu bar, Finder right-click, or folder monitoring. Custom presets set compression levels, which the page describes as six levels. Compression runs locally and the page states images are not uploaded.
notable: Local processing with no image uploads, and works offline
Command-line interface (zipic CLI), installable via Homebrew cask
Notch Drop and clipboard auto-compress on Pro
caveats: Free tier is limited to 25 compressions per day with basic features; full Pro features require a paid license
Pro licenses are priced per device count (1 device, 2 devices, or 10 devices)
